caption: Celnet's adaptable architecture — pluggable market-data and product adapters flow into one celnet-proto contract wrapping a pinned zero-allocation hot core that prices the full catalogue (vanilla, five smile families incl. eSSVI, the 18-product exotic Instrument through American/Bermudan and correlated baskets plus an LSV booking engine), emits bit-identical surfaces across the GUI, Excel, SDK, CLI, WebSocket, FIX and CelNet Trader, scales out over a Raft-replicated log and SPMC fan-out ring, and deploys three ways through reversible adapter swaps behind a conflating egress governor — with an explicit honest boundary on deploy-gated absolutes.
alt: Architecture diagram: inbound vendor and CelNet feeds enter via a market-data seam into a navy Celnet core framed by the single celnet-proto contract (async edge, wait-free rings, pinned hot cores for ingest/surface, pricer/Greeks, risk, GPU/telemetry). The quant-engine band names five smile families including eSSVI and the full 18-product exotic catalogue (digitals, touches, eight barriers, var/vol swaps, Asian, forward-start/cliquet, quanto, TARF, accumulator, lookback, American/Bermudan, basket/best-of/worst-of, LSV booking model) with per-class validation; the plugin band shows Tier-0 native and Tier-2 wasmi as shipped and Tier-1 signed-.so / Tier-3 OS-sandbox as designed and deploy-gated. caption: Celnet exposes one clean, unversioned contract served by the Celnet server and fanned out to six surfaces — gRPC, a byte-identical WebSocket JSON mirror, the Rust client SDK, the CLI, the 27-function Excel CELNET.* add-in, and the React/WebGPU GUI — carrying a unified 18-product exotic Instrument, the VV/SABR/SVI/SSVI/eSSVI smile-model selector, surface marking and the RiskService roll-up with limits, so the front-end uses the same APIs as any client and every value is bit-identical (Monte-Carlo products returning a price standard error) across them all.
alt: Architecture diagram showing a central coral-marked Celnet contract hub fanning out to six client surfaces (gRPC, byte-identical WebSocket mirror, Rust SDK, CLI, 27-function Excel add-in, React/WebGPU GUI), each labelled same contract and value bit-identical, with the contract carrying pricing, quote/RFQ, multiplex stream, the unified 18-product Instrument (vanilla through American/Bermudan and multi-asset basket), surface marking with the VV/SABR/SVI/SSVI/eSSVI smile-model selector, the market-series feed, the RiskService roll-up plus limits, and attribution identity, with a footnote that Monte-Carlo products carry a price standard error rather than machine precision.

caption: Celnet's quant and pricing methodology coverage — Garman-Kohlhagen vanilla with the full FX desk Greek set (FD- and AAD-validated), the volatility smile and arbitrage-free surface engine (Vanna-Volga, SABR, SVI, SSVI and eSSVI, with a Dupire local-vol surface and LSV booking model), and a full exotic, structured and multi-asset catalogue — barriers, digitals, touches, Asian, lookback, forward-start/cliquet, variance/volatility swaps, TARF, accumulator, quanto, American/Bermudan (PSOR free-boundary FD and Longstaff-Schwartz LSM) and Cholesky-correlated basket/best-of/worst-of — priced by complementary analytic, PDE, Monte-Carlo and survival-VV methods over a Sobol'/Brownian-bridge QMC engine. Analytic, PDE and golden classes are validated to machine precision against frozen QuantLib golden tables (vanilla, digital, barrier, double-barrier, touch, Heston); structured, MC, American, basket and LSV products carry an honest Monte-Carlo standard error and are checked against closed-form limits and ~26 parity rows vs independent oracles. Extensible via the Open Quant SDK plugin host (native Tier-0 and wasmi Tier-2).
alt: Three-column architecture diagram: Vanilla and Greeks; Smile and Surface (five smile models plus Dupire local-vol and LSV booking); and a grouped full catalogue (vanilla family, path-dependent, structured/MC, early-exercise American/Bermudan, and Cholesky multi-asset basket/rainbow) with a method legend and Monte-Carlo standard-error tags, over a band noting frozen-golden-table and ~26-parity-row validation, an honest MC-standard-error and GPU-ratio boundary footnote, and SDK extensibility.

caption: Celnet's surface pipeline turns broker ATM and risk-reversal/butterfly quotes into a versioned, arbitrage-free marked surface — market-to-smile strangle calibration, a switchable five-family smile-model selector (VV, SABR, SVI, SSVI and eSSVI), and butterfly, calendar and vertical no-arbitrage gates — which pricing, RFQ and RFS consume by pinned version, rejecting any unknown version rather than silently falling back to live.
alt: Left-to-right surface construction pipeline from broker quotes through strangle calibration, a five-family smile-model selector (VV, SABR, SVI, SSVI, eSSVI) and arbitrage gates to a versioned marked surface, with an official-versus-live registry below where pricing paths pin a surface version and unknown versions are rejected.

caption: Celnet's Open Quant SDK: one frozen trait contract and a tier-blind model registry route every model through the same calling convention — the Native (Tier-0) and WebAssembly-sandbox (Tier-2 wasmi) tiers are shipped and gated, while the signed-shared-object (Tier-1) and OS-sandbox (Tier-3 Landlock/seccomp) tiers are designed-and-seamed behind the same contract and proven at deploy — with only the core math primitives crossing a zero-ambient-authority capability boundary and a built-in butterfly no-arbitrage self-check, so desks run private-IP custom models in-engine, extending an already-complete catalogue (five smile families, the full exotic & structured set through American/Bermudan and correlated baskets, plus an LSV booking model) without forking Celnet.

caption: Celnet's risk architecture spans book-shaped scenario risk — real repricing across a spot-vol shock grid, bucketed vega, cross-gamma and theta-roll horizons against versioned marked surfaces (VV/SABR/SVI/SSVI/eSSVI) — and a firm-wide OLAP position-fact cube where vanilla and exotic legs roll up over eight axes with convention-canonicalized netting, non-additive VaR/ES and FRTB-SA curvature, cascading limits, entitlement pruning and internal-only XVA (CVA/DVA/FVA over synthetic netting sets), with Book and Risk two zooms of one cube exposed identically to GUI, SDK and Excel.

caption: Celnet's node-local hot substrate prices investment-bank-sized portfolios in-core, while a highest-random-weight partition map shards the book across the fleet, a full Raft-replicated log (election, conflicting-tail truncation, compaction and InstallSnapshot) gives bit-identical replay and hot-standby takeover, cross-fleet risk fans out to equal the single-node aggregate to 1e-12, and a conflating egress governor over a lock-free SPMC fan-out ring streams continuous two-way prices to many high-performance counterparties — with an explicit honest boundary that cross-host wire p99, cross-DC transport, dynamic membership and absolute wire SLOs are deploy/live-gated (in-repo proofs are loopback / localhost-multiprocess).
alt: Two-zone architecture diagram. Zone A, the node-local hot substrate, shows the async edge feeding pinned zero-allocation hot cores over wait-free SPSC rings, lock-free read-mostly state (atomic snapshot swap, seqlock top-of-book, cache-padded counters), blue-green handoff with a durable checksummed journal, many-instrument many-tenor batched repricing computing the full FX desk Greek set in one pass, a cross-platform GPU pricing backend (Metal / Vulkan / DX12 with an f64 CPU oracle and SIMD fallback, batch closed-form, path-MC, pathwise/LR Greeks and Sobol-QMC kernels reconciled f32-to-f64), and zero-cost observability. caption: Celnet's multi-asset coverage built on the carry-producing-market architecture (ADR-0008): three orthogonal layers — an Underlying identity union (the only place asset class is named), a Carry layer that produces the forward and discount so FX two-rate, equity (r,q), commodity (r,convenience) and crypto (r,funding) all collapse to generalized-BSM F=S·e^(b·t), and asset-class-AGNOSTIC payoff engines that consume only forward/discount/surface so a new asset class is a new carry builder with zero payoff-engine edits — radiating out to the asset-class superset: FX (deliverable + NDF) live and gate-validated, with precious metals (XAU/XAG/XPT/XPD + crosses, lease-rate carry), digital-assets/crypto (linear and inverse/coin-settled with a 24×7 clock and funding carry), equity/index (dividend + repo) and commodity (Black-76, convenience yield) as cross-asset capability plus a designed rates seam, the linear book (forward/swap/NDF as priced products), structured Pivot and multi-dealer RFQ aggregation, and a cross-asset factor-keyed risk fact feeding FRTB-SA GIRR/equity/commodity/CSR buckets in one firm book.
alt: A capability landscape diagram centred on the navy three-layer carry-producing-market architecture: layer 1 Identity (the Underlying discriminated union plus settlement style, the only place asset class is named), arrow down to layer 2 Market (the Carry producer emitting forward(t) and discount(t), with FX two-rate, equity r-q, commodity r-convenience and crypto r-funding all collapsing to generalized-BSM F equals S times e to the b t), arrow down to layer 3 Payoff (asset-class-agnostic vanilla/barrier/Asian engines consuming only forward, discount and a surface, so a new asset class needs zero payoff-engine edits), with a note that no payoff engine branches on the carry variant. Radiating to the right is the asset-class superset: a green Live FX panel (deliverable plus NDF, 19-pair panel growing past 75, five smile families, full exotic catalogue) and capability tiles for precious metals (XAU/XAG/XPT/XPD plus crosses, loco-London, lease-rate carry), digital-assets/crypto (linear USD-T generalized-BSM and the inverse/coin-settled 1/S_T payoff, 24×7 continuous clock, funding carry b equals r minus funding), equity/index (dividend plus repo carry, dividend-rho, strike/moneyness surface), commodity (Black-76 on the listed future, convenience-yield carry, futures-settled) and a dashed designed rates seam (Bachelier normal vol, curve-bucketed rho). A bottom band shows the linear book (FX outright forward, FX swap near plus far, NDF cash-settled at fixing as priced discounted-cashflow products), structured plus workflow (Pivot as a TARF generalization, perpetual and listed-future options, the multi-dealer RFQ panel ranking best bid/offer with deterministic tie-break and last-look), and cross-asset risk (a generalized factor-keyed risk fact feeding FRTB-SA GIRR, equity, commodity and CSR buckets, the additive-merge and non-additive re-gather algebra netting every class into one firm cube with fan-out equal to single-node). A dashed footnote states FX is the live gate-validated class while the non-FX leaves are cross-asset capability on the same carry seam validated against independent oracles, and lists deploy-gated items: live crypto/metal fixing and lease-rate values, live funding-rate feeds, live LP-panel connectivity and regulated-venue MAS-RMO status, and live equity dividend/repo and commodity convenience curves.

caption: The carry-model abstraction at the heart of Celnet's multi-asset architecture (ADR-0008): every asset class maps its native inputs into a single generalized-BSM forward F = S·e^(b·t) and discount df = e^(−r·t), with FX (r = r_dom, b = r_dom − r_for, reproduced bit-for-bit), equity (b = r − q − repo), commodity (b = r − convenience, the listed-future Black-76 case b = 0), crypto (b = r − funding) and metals (b = r − lease) differing only in how the carry rate b is assembled from named factors — so the asset-class-agnostic payoff engines (vanilla through American/Bermudan and baskets) consume only the forward, discount and surface and the payoff code never branches on asset class, with a binding no-workaround rule, a multi-curve-ready seam and a typed INVALID_ARGUMENT validity matrix rather than any silent fallback.
alt: Three-column flow diagram. On the left, five asset-class carry builders each show how they assemble the carry rate b for the generalized-BSM core: FX (green, r equals r_dom and b equals r_dom minus r_for, reproducing the Garman-Kohlhagen forward and both discount factors bit-for-bit), equity/index (b equals r minus q minus repo), commodity (b equals r minus convenience, with the listed-future Black-76 case b equals 0), crypto/digital asset (b equals r minus funding, 24x7 clock) and metals (b equals r minus lease, loco-London T+2). An arrow feeds a central navy generalized-BSM core box stating forward F equals S times e to the b times t and discount df equals e to the minus r times t, with forward(t) and discount(t) chips and the note that a new asset class is a new carry builder while the payoff side never changes. A second arrow feeds an indigo asset-class-agnostic payoff-engines box listing vanilla, barrier, digital, touch, Asian, lookback, variance/vol swap, forward-start/cliquet, quanto, TARF, accumulator, American/Bermudan and basket, all consuming only forward, discount and a vol surface, tagged payoff code never names the asset class. A centred note says asset class is named in exactly one place, the Underlying identity, and carry is a forward/discount producer not a variant. A lower band gives the binding no-workaround test (a match on the carry variant in payoff code is a review blocker), multi-curve readiness (OIS/CSA discounting slots behind the same forward/discount interface) and no-silent-mis-pricing (a product-by-underlying validity matrix yields a typed INVALID_ARGUMENT, clients default to FX). A footnote reconciles zero-alloc with general: the hot-core Greeks keep a fixed POD shape with a small rate-sensitivity enum while FRTB factor decomposition into GIRR/equity/commodity/CSR buckets happens off the hot path, with rho_dom equals discount_rho plus carry_rho and rho_for equals minus carry_rho recovered by the AAD adjoint.

caption: Celnet's digital-asset settlement and carry, on the ADR-0008 carry seam: a linear / USD(T)-margined contract is exactly generalized-BSM (the leaf assembles the funding cost-of-carry b = r − funding, F = S·e^(b·t), and calls the shared asset-class-agnostic engine with zero new payoff math), while the inverse / coin-margined contract is a genuinely new payoff shape whose 1/S_T factor — premium and payoff denominated in the base coin — introduces a real convexity/measure subtlety priced by a numeraire change into the coin/share measure (V_coin = (φ/S₀)·e^(−b·t)·(N(φd₁) − (K/F)·N(φd₂))) with coin-measure delta/gamma/vega rather than silently the USD ones; the 24×7 continuous trading clock (no weekend skip, no holiday centres, exchange-fixed UTC expiry) sits beside a three-way validation that always keeps an oracle able to disagree with the closed form — an independent Gauss–Hermite quadrature, a code-disjoint splitmix64 Monte-Carlo of the raw 1/S_T payoff gated within its reported standard error, and the structural sandwich V_inverse·S₀ > V_lin — surfaced bit-identically across GUI, SDK, CLI, Excel and the WebSocket mirror, with an explicit honest boundary that live venue connectivity, vol-surface/option-chain values, index-price fixings and funding-rate values are deploy-gated (ENV) while the payoff math, measure correctness, convention identity and carry assembly are proven in-repo.
alt: Two-track diagram of Celnet's digital-asset/crypto settlement on the ADR-0008 carry seam. The left track, linear / USD(T)-margined, shows the leaf assembling the funding cost-of-carry b equals r minus funding, forming the generalized-BSM forward F equals S times e to the b t, and calling the shared asset-class-agnostic vanilla engine with zero new payoff math. The right track, inverse / coin-margined, shows the genuinely new payoff shape with a one-over-S-T factor, premium and payoff denominated in the base coin, priced by a numeraire change into the coin/share measure with the closed form V_coin equals phi over S-zero times e to the minus b t times the quantity N of phi d-one minus K over F times N of phi d-two, reporting coin-measure delta, gamma and vega rather than USD ones. A clock panel shows the 24x7 continuous trading calendar with no weekend skip, no holiday centres and exchange-fixed UTC expiry. A validation panel shows three independent oracles that can disagree with the closed form: an independent Gauss-Hermite quadrature, a code-disjoint splitmix64 Monte-Carlo of the raw one-over-S-T payoff gated within its reported standard error, and a structural sandwich V_inverse times S-zero greater than V_linear. A client band shows the result bit-identical across GUI, SDK, CLI, Excel and the WebSocket mirror. A dashed footnote states the honest boundary: live venue connectivity, vol-surface and option-chain values, index-price fixings and funding-rate values are deploy-gated by environment, while the payoff math, measure correctness, convention identity and carry assembly are proven in-repo.

caption: Celnet's cross-asset risk architecture nets every asset class into one firm book over factor-keyed facts: the pinned zero-allocation hot core emits the full FX desk Greek set in a fixed Copy/POD shape (delta-vs-underlying, vega, discount-rho, carry-rho — a small fixed enum, never an allocating factor map), and a risk-layer projection off the hot path decomposes those rate sensitivities into FRTB-bucketed factors per class (FX live; equity dividend/repo, commodity convenience-yield, and a designed crypto/rates seam), with asset class named in exactly one place. Each leg flows as an immutable factor-keyed fact into the eight-axis hierarchical position-fact cube, where an additive per-factor roll-up that never reads the asset-class tag nets across all classes alongside non-additive VaR/ES and FRTB-SbM curvature re-gathered per node, projecting into the class-agnostic SbM machine over GIRR/FX/equity/commodity/CSR buckets, pruned by entitlements and a cascading limit tree, and collapsing to one cross-asset firm book exposed identically to GUI, SDK and Excel — proving firm_aggregate == single-node to 1e-12 (1e-9 for re-gathered non-additive measures) against an independent recomputation, with the existing FX parity staying byte-green. FX is the live gate-validated class; non-FX leaves are cross-asset capability on the same carry seam validated vs independent oracles, while live dividend/repo/convenience/funding curves and FRTB risk-weights/correlations are caller-supplied deploy-gated data and FX deliverable DRC is an honest zero.
alt: Left-to-right cross-asset risk pipeline. On the left, the pinned zero-allocation hot core emits the full FX desk Greek set in a fixed Copy/POD shape: delta-versus-underlying, vega, discount-rho and carry-rho, labelled a small fixed enum and never an allocating factor map. An arrow to a risk-layer projection, drawn off the hot path, decomposes the rate sensitivities into FRTB-bucketed factors per asset class: FX live in green, with equity dividend and repo, commodity convenience yield, and a dashed designed crypto and rates seam, annotated that asset class is named in exactly one place. Each leg becomes an immutable factor-keyed fact flowing into the eight-axis hierarchical position-fact cube, where an additive per-factor roll-up that never reads the asset-class tag nets across all classes, alongside non-additive VaR, ES and FRTB-SbM curvature re-gathered per node. These project into the class-agnostic Sensitivities-Based-Method machine over GIRR, FX, equity, commodity and CSR buckets, pruned by entitlements and a cascading limit tree, and collapse into one cross-asset firm book exposed identically to GUI, SDK and Excel. A proof badge states firm_aggregate equals single-node to 1e-12, and 1e-9 for re-gathered non-additive measures, against an independent recomputation, with existing FX parity staying byte-green. A dashed footnote states FX is the live gate-validated class while non-FX leaves are cross-asset capability on the same carry seam validated against independent oracles, and that live dividend, repo, convenience and funding curves and FRTB risk-weights and correlations are caller-supplied deploy-gated data, and FX deliverable DRC is an honest zero.

caption: Celnet's multi-dealer RFQ aggregation — the multi-bank-venue answer to a single-dealer incumbent: one client QuoteRequest fans out concurrently over an object-safe QuoteSource panel to N quote sources — an always-present internal Celnet pricer plus external FIX LP adapters over the celnet-fix 4.4 initiator engine — each returning a two-way (bid/offer with epoch and valid_until). The engine ranks them identically into best-bid (highest premium) and best-offer (lowest premium) with a deterministic earliest-epoch-then-smallest-LP-id tie-break, drops timed-out non-responders and rejects last-look-stale winners (promoting the next-best), then books exactly the ranked winner by (quote_id, lp_id) over the same keyed line-bound token path as click-to-trade/FIX, with lp_count/lp_won consistency (every lp_won is a responder) gated against an injected ground-truth ladder; one ranked panel is bit-identical across GUI, SDK, CLI and Excel, while live LP-panel connectivity and regulated-venue/MAS-RMO status are deploy-gated (in-repo proves the aggregation/ranking/tie-break/last-look algorithm plus FIX framing over a loopback initiator/acceptor pair).
alt: A fan-out and fan-in diagram of Celnet's multi-dealer RFQ aggregation. On the left, one client QuoteRequest fans out concurrently over an object-safe QuoteSource panel to N quote sources: an always-present internal Celnet pricer plus several external FIX liquidity-provider adapters over the celnet-fix 4.4 initiator engine, each returning a two-way bid and offer with an epoch and a valid_until. In the centre, a ranking engine sorts them into best bid as the highest premium and best offer as the lowest premium, applies a deterministic tie-break of earliest epoch then smallest LP id, drops timed-out non-responders and rejects last-look-stale winners while promoting the next best. On the right, the engine books exactly the ranked winner by quote id and LP id over the same keyed line-bound token path as click-to-trade and FIX, with an lp_count and lp_won consistency check stating every lp_won is a responder, gated against an injected ground-truth ladder. A client band shows one ranked panel bit-identical across GUI, SDK, CLI and Excel. A dashed footnote states live LP-panel connectivity and regulated-venue MAS-RMO status are deploy-gated, while in-repo proves the aggregation, ranking, tie-break and last-look algorithm plus FIX framing over a loopback initiator and acceptor pair.

caption: Celnet's state-of-the-art evolution model: one clean, unversioned contract evolved in place with zero legacy (no schema_version, no version negotiation, generalize-and-delete behind a byte-identical no-regression gate); the architectural leap to cross-asset via three orthogonal layers (ADR-0008) — an Underlying identity union as the only place asset class is named, a Carry forward/discount producer where FX two-rate, equity (r,q), commodity convenience and crypto funding all collapse to generalized cost-of-carry F = S·e^(b·t), and asset-class-agnostic payoff engines so a new asset class is a new carry builder with zero payoff-engine edits; an executable conformance regime of engine-generated golden vectors cross-checked by independent oracles (QuantLib golden tables, published closed forms, code-disjoint Monte-Carlo) and a five-client (gRPC/SDK/CLI/Excel/GUI) real-edge harness from which the parity matrix is generated; and a continuous evolution loop — seven critique lenses → compose the latest research as a method or disjoint leaf → verify against an oracle and parity gate → converge until two dry rounds — that feeds back onto the same single contract without rewrite, with a verbatim honest boundary on deploy-gated absolutes.
alt: A four-band vertical diagram of Celnet's state-of-the-art evolution model. Band one, one unversioned contract, shows a single clean contract evolved in place with zero legacy: no schema_version, no version negotiation, generalize-and-delete behind a byte-identical no-regression gate. Band two, the cross-asset architectural leap from ADR-0008, shows three orthogonal layers stacked: an Underlying identity union labelled the only place asset class is named, a Carry forward and discount producer where FX two-rate, equity r and q, commodity convenience and crypto funding all collapse to the generalized cost-of-carry forward F equals S times e to the b t, and asset-class-agnostic payoff engines, annotated that a new asset class is a new carry builder with zero payoff-engine edits. Band three, executable conformance, shows engine-generated golden vectors cross-checked by independent oracles that can disagree — QuantLib golden tables, published closed forms and code-disjoint Monte-Carlo — feeding a five-client real-edge harness over gRPC, SDK, CLI, Excel and GUI, from which the parity matrix is generated. Band four, the continuous evolution loop, is a cycle: seven critique lenses, then compose the latest research as a method or a disjoint leaf, then verify against an oracle and the parity gate, then converge until two dry rounds, with an arrow feeding back onto the same single contract without rewrite. A dashed footnote carries the verbatim honest boundary on deploy-gated absolutes.
